description.purpose: The colony shell: the outermost of the four composition levels, and the tree everything else is grown into. It is authored under one rule that all four levels repeat in the same words -- A LEVEL OWNS WHAT ITS SIBLINGS MUST SHARE. What every organisation of a colony shares is the capability broker, the control loop, -- since R6 -- the ONE authoring path a colony has (the baumeister that drafts a manifest and the submitter that carries it to the mutation door under the requester's own identity), and -- since 1.3.0 -- the ONE front door a person addresses it through (`operator`, GH #446). Those five stood here as refs through 1.6.1; since 1.7.0 there are four, the submitter having moved inside the front door (#556). They are pinned to exact versions; beside them stands `orgs`, a real but empty container hive. The shell holds no cell of its own, no memory, no model and no state: it routes fourteen lanes in, sixteen lanes out, and owns the boundary. Since 1.3.2 the control-loop ref is `argus@1.1.0`, renamed from `steward` (GH #462), and the rename brought ONE lane with it: `alert`, a watched symptom the loop's meter counted deterministically with no model asked. Nothing at this level can act on it, so the shell does the one honest thing it can -- it draws the exit and hands it out, because a level that drains nothing loses every warning. Since 1.4.0 ([#458](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/458)) one more lane crosses outward: `pack_ack`, the receipt of an identity pushed into a generation below. Nothing at this level consumes it, so by the union rule it has to be declared and let out -- adding an emitted lane is the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a). Since 1.5.0 ([#469](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/469)) the thirteenth inbound lane is `in_build`, and declaring it RETRACTS half of what this file said through 1.4.0. The sentence was: the builder lane pair is deliberately not at the rim, because `./orgs` raises it and `./builder` takes it, so it crosses nothing -- the lane is invisible from outside precisely because the baumeister stands inside. That reading is still true of `build` and `in_build_result`, which are an assistant's names for the same round. It was wrong about the one case it had to be right about: the FIRST build of a colony, where `./orgs` is empty by construction and no assistant exists to raise anything, so the road the whole argument rested on has no traveller. `in_build` is the operator's name for that round and it reaches the rim; the level's own door stamps `context.build_caller`, and the draft comes back to the front door instead of into the empty container. Adding an inbound lane a caller could never reach before is the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a). Since 1.6.0 ([#504](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/504)) a fifteenth edge wires two occupants to each other and a fourteenth lane crosses outward, and they are one decision. `./submit -> ./builder`, guarded on a receipt that carries no `error_code` and on `hop.registers_class`, re-stamps the round onto `in_ingest`: the submitter is the ONE cell in the tree that knows both that a manifest committed and that its diff registered a class, and the baumeister's corpus is a seed that stops describing the library the moment one does. The documented wiring named `./submit/gate -> ./builder/librarian` and no manifest, operator or hand-written config could draw it -- both endpoints are interior nodes of sealed hives -- so the lane moved to the two hive paths, where it is drawable. `catalogue` is the report coming back out; the baumeister pairs the two in its own `required_drains`, and adding an emitted lane is the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a), the same reading `pack_ack` got in 1.4.0. Since 1.6.1 the baumeister ref is pinned to `builder@1.5.2`, which renamed two of its own occupants after the templates they reference (#545). Nothing at this level moved but the pin. Since 1.7.0 ([#556](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/556)) the shell holds FOUR refs and not five: the submitter stopped being a shell-level hive and became an occupant of the front door (`/os/operator/submit`), and the whole of what this level lost with it is a station. One front, one place a submission lives, and a road readable off the graph -- a submission used to cross `./operator` and then `./submit` for what is one job. Six edges of this level moved: `./operator -> ./submit` on `apply` and `./submit -> ./operator` on `receipt` are INTERIOR to the front door now and are not this level's business at all, while `./submit -> ./access` on `ask`, `./access -> ./submit` on `grant`, `./submit -> .` on `mutate` and the two `./submit -> ./builder` nudges of 1.6.0 are drawn from `./operator` instead -- same guards, same lanes, one hive further out. The requester the ask edge stamps moved with the node it names: `/os/operator/submit`, because R-AC-1 rules the identity of the node whose reach the rule is about, and a rule naming the front door as a whole would permit more than the submitter is. Nothing this level DECLARES changed -- thirteen lanes in, fifteen out -- because the union rule cancels exactly what moved inside: `ask`, `sub_receipt` and `in_verdict` cross the operator rim and are consumed by a sibling of this level, so no lane of them reaches this one. Removing an occupant and rewiring its edges is the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a). And it does NOT reach a running colony: the `mutate` lane lives in the birth topology, so a colony adopts this with its next instance and keeps its grown form otherwise (no-delete). Since 1.8.0 the fourteenth inbound lane is `mutation_committed` (GH #553): the mutation door leaves one receipt per committed knock at the hive `colony.json` names, and this level carries it into `./orgs`. Declaring it is what makes this level a mandatory hop for the lane (ADR-0020) -- the chain is drawn one level at a time, all the way down to the tool menus and the screens that used to poll for the same fact. Since #555 a sixteenth lane crosses outward: `dump`, the receipt of one applied import part on its way out of a member and its organisation. Nothing at this level consumes it, so by the union rule it has to be declared and let out -- it used to end inside the member, in the one cell there that read a transfer document and said nothing about it. Since 1.8.1 the rollup asks the environment for ELEVEN keys instead of twenty-nine: the authoring dispatcher's three knobs, the control loop's seven, the capability broker's six and the two source names of the vault inside it are params of the cells that read them ([#138](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/138)) -- `dispatcher@1.2.0`, `argus@1.1.0` and `access@2.5.0` -- so a key set for any of them in the environment would go nowhere, and an `override_params` entry in the manifest that grows the shell is what tunes them now. `requires.env` is derived from what the refs actually substitute, and a key that binds nothing is a leaflet -- so it goes.
description.use_when: Once per colony, as the first thing an operator instantiates. Everything else arrives afterwards as an organisation instantiated into `./orgs`, and the mutation that grows one draws that organisation's own edges in the same breath. Do not instantiate a second shell into a colony that already has one: two brokers mean two answers to the same question, and two control loops mean two hands on the same params.
description.not_in_scope: No `turn` lane outward: the level declares the UNION of what its occupants emit, minus what a sibling inside consumes itself -- and a member consumes its own turn behind its screen (`./assistants -> ./firewall`), so an exit for it here could never fire. No second vault: `access` carries its own interior one and the standalone `vault` template attests its inbound edges against `params.broker` plus `params.sealed_neighbors`, so a copy at this level would boot locked and inert (ruling Q20, GH #302). No swallowing sink: nothing here accepts a refusal and emits nothing, because the dead-letter queue is the record (ruling Q2, GH #284). No `connect` lane outward: `access` requires that lane to be the ONE edge that reaches a connector cell, and that edge is drawn where the connector stands, not here. No contract on the container: the level declares the transit lanes and its own edges satisfy them from birth (W7-R2). No organisation-level anything -- the shell ships the container, never a tenant. And no slot: the substrate's slot governs an address that does not exist, while `orgs` does exist, so the declaration would have been silent and the `params.ports` it needs would have SEALED this hive. And NO SECOND BAUMEISTER and no second front door: two of either would be two audit trails, and the one audit trail is the whole point of R6. And no submitter of this level's own since 1.7.0: the one that exists lives inside the front door (#556), and a second one here would be the second privileged edge R6 was written to prevent. No authentication either -- the front door supplies an identity and never verifies a claim; that is a reverse proxy's job in front of the API, and the broker's behind it.
examples: LANES - the hive path is the address and `hop.route` is the lane; `params.ports` is ABSENT, which is the open state, and no edge from outside is refused by a boundary this level does not draw. in_request and in_invoke reach the broker and both demand a promoted `context.requester`; in_cycle reaches the control loop; in_turn, in_recall, in_brief and in_propose reach the `orgs` container; in_build reaches the baumeister; in_submit, in_dump and in_lifecycle reach the front door, and in_export and in_import reach the `orgs` container. grant, ack, mutate, alert, answer, bundle (the answer to a question asked at a member's own in_recall door, GH #533 -- the question has crossed this level since it was written and the answer had no exit at any of the three levels it has to leave), reject, error, receipt, write, turn_write, prune, close_report, pack_ack and catalogue leave the hive path -- `turn` does NOT, because a member consumes its own turn behind its screen. Nothing addresses an occupant by name from outside: the occupants are refs, and their interiors belong to their own templates.

THE FOUR REFS - `access`, `argus`, `builder` and `operator`, each pinned to an exact version in its own ref file rather than named bare. A bare name resolves to the newest version on disk, so a shell that shipped one would silently adopt a new broker the day a bump landed -- which is precisely the drift `registry.template_chain` exists to make visible, not to excuse. The chain a grown node carries reads outermost-first: `meclaw-os` and then the occupant's own template. The fifth was `submit` and it is one storey down since 1.7.0 (#556): the submitter is an occupant of `operator`, and a chain that reaches its gate now reads `meclaw-os`, `operator`, `submit`.

THE CONTAINER - `orgs` is a real hive with no children, no edges and no `params` block at all. Real, because #303 forces the same shape one level further down (`channels` must be a node to carry its fan-in edges once) and four levels with one shape beat four levels with three. Empty, because an organisation is instantiated INTO it. Open, because the instantiating mutation draws edges to that organisation and a sealed hive refuses exactly those endpoints. And SILENT, because a contract on an empty hive declares doors that lead nowhere: the level declares the organisation's own lanes instead -- six in, nine out -- and its own fifteen edges to and from `./orgs` satisfy the door-and-exit check from birth (W7-R2).

THE ARGUS TALKS TO THE COLONY - since GH #267 the control loop asks `/colony/ledger` for its numbers instead of opening a database it does not own. Two absolute lanes, `./meter` and `./probe` onto that endpoint, travel with the ref: this shell writes no edge for them and must not seal them away. The virtual endpoints are in bounds at every scope, so wrapping the loop one level deeper changes nothing about them.

IT DECIDES NOTHING - the whole level is transit. The shell has no cell, so it cannot compute, refuse or remember; `builder` and `operator` are refs, not cells of the shell, and that sentence stays true. The edges that wire two occupants to each other rather than to the rim are the interesting ones -- that is what OWNING an authoring path and a front door looks like, and it is the same shape `assistant` uses for `./cogny -> ./tools`. A level that grew one of those would have stopped being a boundary and started being a participant.

THE SUBMITTER ASKS THE BROKER - two of those edges are the pair `./operator -> ./access` on `ask` and `./access -> ./operator` on `grant`, and only this level can draw them: the submitter now stands INSIDE the front door and the broker is the front door's sibling, so the question leaves one hive and enters another and both crossings are this level's. The outward edge stamps `context.requester` to `/os/operator/submit`, because the broker reads the requester from the EDGE and never from a body (R-AC-1) -- the identity on whose behalf it asks travels as `subject` inside the question. It names the OCCUPANT and not the hive around it: the reach the rule is about belongs to the submitter, and `/os/operator` would permit an export cell and a lifecycle composer the same thing. The stamp is honest because `ask` has exactly one sender inside that hive, which `operator@1.1.0` declares. The edge also promotes the manifest digest into `context.sub_sha`, since `hop.*` lives for exactly one hop and the answer has to be matched back against it. The marker `sub_ask` is in the SUBMITTER's key space, not the broker's `ac_*`, which the broker overwrites on its own internal edges -- and the rim edge for `grant` excludes it, because edges fan out and a verdict for the submitter is not an answer the outside asked for.

THE FRONT DOOR - `operator` is the fourth ref and the answer to the one thing a POST does not carry: a sender. The substrate stamps `reply_to` on a CELL's emission, so an agent inside the colony is attributable and a person with a shell is not; a request that becomes a message emitted by an occupant of that hive has a path, and the submitter's gate stops refusing operator submissions as anonymous. Since 1.7.0 the gate is that hive's own occupant, so the two edges that used to carry a manifest out to `./submit` and a receipt back are gone from this file entirely (#556). Five edges of this level wire the front door to its siblings: `./orgs -> ./operator` on an agent's `build` with `build_op == 'apply'` and on `export_done`; `./operator -> ./orgs` carrying an agent's receipt home as `in_build_result` and the export trigger down as `in_export`; and `./builder -> ./operator` on `manifest`, since 1.5.0 -- a draft an OPERATOR asked for, guarded on `context.build_caller` so it is the only class of draft that takes it. One submission front door means one, and a manifest the baumeister drew for a person has to arrive at the same door the person's hand-written one does -- digest, gate and broker included. It gives IDENTITY and never AUTHENTICATION: no token, no header check, nothing of the kind reaches this level or the one below it.

THE OPERATOR DRIVES THE BAUMEISTER - stage two, for a colony that has nothing in it yet (GH #469). `in_build` at the rim, `context.build_caller` stamped by this level's door, the draft back out through `./builder -> ./operator` as `in_submit`, and a failure back out through `./builder -> .` as `error`. The two old `./builder -> ./orgs` edges carry the counter-guard, so an assistant's round still goes home to its own organisation and an operator's is never delivered twice -- edges fan out, and a lane with two destinations and no discriminator is two deliveries. What this does NOT decide is whether the submission is permitted: the shipped policy row `colony.mutate.default` scopes an agent's mutations to `/os/orgs`, so a first ORGANISATION -- whose scope is necessarily `/os` -- comes back as a named `requester_not_permitted` rather than as a silent dead letter, and growing the OS shell itself stays an operator act at `/colony/mutations`. Turning `hive_no_route` into an answer is the whole of what the wiring buys; which answers are given is the broker's business.

THE CORPUS IS NUDGED BY THE ONE CELL THAT KNOWS - `./operator -> ./builder` on `sub_receipt` with no `error_code` and `hop.registers_class == true`, re-stamped `in_ingest`, and `./builder -> .` on `catalogue` carrying the report back out (GH #504). The lane out of the front door is `sub_receipt` and not `receipt` since #556: the submitter's own words, let out only when they carry a fact the front door cannot answer for, because a submission answered on `receipt` twice is a submission whose caller cannot tell which answer is the outcome. Only this level can draw the edge, for the reason it is the only one that can draw `./operator -> ./access`: the front door and the baumeister are siblings here and nowhere else. Both guards are load-bearing -- `registers_class` alone would nudge after a manifest that registered a class and was refused at the door, and `committed` alone would nudge after every submission a colony ever makes. Nothing here subscribes to the report: it leaves as a lane, like `alert` and `pack_ack`, and `seed-ref` draws no edge for it (ruling Q2, GH #284).

ARGUS_JUDGE_BASE_URL.because: binds `params.base_url` of the loop's `judge`, written `${ARGUS_JUDGE_BASE_URL:-https://openrouter.ai/api/v1}`. Any OpenAI-shaped endpoint serves; `provider` names the wire protocol, never the vendor

ARGUS_JUDGE_MODEL.because: binds `params.model` of the loop's `judge`, written `${ARGUS_JUDGE_MODEL:-anthropic/claude-opus-4}`. This is the one cell in the colony where a weaker model is a false economy: it decides what the colony does to itself

ARGUS_JUDGE_PROVIDER.because: binds `params.provider` of the loop's `judge`, written `${ARGUS_JUDGE_PROVIDER:-openai}` — the wire protocol the endpoint speaks

LOCAL_LLM_API_KEY.because: binds `params.api_key` of the builder's `compose` cell, written `${LOCAL_LLM_API_KEY:-}`. Not required, because an empty credential is an ABSENT one and the `llm` cell then sends no `Authorization` header at all (GH #271) — which is exactly right for a loopback endpoint that wants none. It carries no value in this tree and never should: the token is the name of a secret, not the secret

LOCAL_LLM_BASE_URL.because: binds `params.base_url` of the builder's `compose` cell, written `${LOCAL_LLM_BASE_URL:-}`. Unset, the composer has no endpoint to ask and the authoring path drafts nothing — see MODEL_BUILDER for why that is declared rather than required

MODEL_BUILDER.because: binds `params.model` of the builder's `compose` cell, written `${MODEL_BUILDER:-}`. Declared and NOT required, and both halves are deliberate. Declared, because it is the one key that decides whether stage two can happen at all: unset, the shell still boots, the front door still answers and the submitter still gates, but the composer has no model, so a manifest is never drafted and the colony can only be grown by a manifest somebody wrote by hand. Not required, because the config gives it an empty default and requiring here what the cell defaults there would be two contracts disagreeing about one value — the same reading `templates/tools` applies to its own endpoints. Set it, together with LOCAL_LLM_BASE_URL, before the first authoring round

OPENROUTER_API_KEY.because: binds `params.api_key` of the control loop's `judge`, and it is the ONE value in this shell written with no default: `${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}`. A colony that grows this shell without it is refused with `requirement_missing` before a single byte is staged, which is the whole point of this block — the alternative is a shell that boots, looks healthy, and fails at the first cycle the loop runs. The token is the name of a secret; no value of it travels in this tree
